Generate GLM-Based Data Generating Mechanism

Source: R/generate_glm_dgm.R
generate_glm_dgm.Rd

Creates a data generating mechanism (DGM) for non-survival outcomes using generalised linear models.

Usage

generate_glm_dgm(
  data,
  factor_vars,
  continuous_vars = NULL,
  outcome_var,
  treatment_var,
  outcome_type = c("binary", "continuous", "count"),
  effect_measure = NULL,
  offset_var = NULL,
  subgroup_vars = NULL,
  subgroup_cuts = NULL,
  model = c("alt", "null"),
  k_treat = 1,
  k_inter = 0,
  adverse_outcome = FALSE,
  n_super = 5000L,
  seed = 8316951L,
  verbose = FALSE,
  k_random_noise = 0L,
  noise_seed = 20260807L
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the source dataset.

factor_vars

Character vector of factor/categorical variable names to include as covariates. These are the candidate confounders for ForestSearch (e.g., paste0("z", 1:12)).

continuous_vars

Character vector of continuous variable names to include as prognostic covariates in the baseline GLM. These improve the model fit but do not participate in subgroup definition. Consistent with generate_aft_dgm_flex, which accepts both continuous_vars and factor_vars. Default NULL (factor-only model, backward compatible).

outcome_var

Character string naming the outcome variable.

treatment_var

Character string naming the treatment variable (must be 0/1 coded).

outcome_type

Character. One of "binary", "continuous", or "count".

effect_measure

Character. Effect measure for the GLM. Default is NULL, which selects "OR" for binary, "MD" for continuous, "IRR" for count outcomes.

offset_var

Character or NULL. Name of the exposure / follow-up time column for count outcomes with an offset. Required when effect_measure is "IRR" or "IRD". The offset enters the Poisson GLM as offset(log(offset_var)). Default NULL.

subgroup_vars

Character vector of variable names defining the subgroup. Default NULL (no subgroup).

subgroup_cuts

Named list of cutpoint specifications for subgroup variables. Uses the same flexible format as generate_aft_dgm_flex: fixed values, quantiles, or functions.

model

Character. "alt" for alternative hypothesis with treatment–subgroup interaction, "null" for uniform treatment effect. Default "alt".

k_treat

Numeric. Scaling factor for the fitted treatment coefficient on the linear predictor scale. k_treat = 1 (default) preserves the fitted treatment effect as-is. k_treat > 1 amplifies the treatment main effect, useful when the source dataset has a weak treatment effect and a stronger ITT is desired for simulation. k_treat < 1 attenuates the effect. Analogous to the k_treat parameter in generate_aft_dgm_flex. Note: the null DGM (model = "null") represents a homogeneous treatment effect (no HTE), not a zero treatment effect. k_treat scales the magnitude of that homogeneous effect.

k_inter

Numeric. Direct additive shift on the linear predictor for Q members under treatment. The interpretation depends on outcome_type:

binary

Shift on the log-odds scale. Positive increases P(Y=1) for Q under treatment.

continuous

Shift on the mean scale (identity link). Positive increases \(E(Y)\) for Q under treatment.

count

Shift on the log-rate scale. Positive increases \(E(Y)\) for Q under treatment (multiplicative: rate multiplied by exp(k_inter)).

Default 0 (no interaction, equivalent to model = "null").

adverse_outcome

Logical. If TRUE and outcome_type = "binary", the interaction shift k_inter is negated internally so that a positive k_inter consistently amplifies the treatment contrast on the beneficial (1 - Y) scale. The flag is stored in the returned object for downstream use by calibrate_glm_interaction and run_simulation_analysis. Default FALSE.

n_super

Integer. Size of the super-population. Default 5000L.

seed

Integer. Random seed for super-population sampling. Default 8316951L.

verbose

Logical. Print diagnostic information. Default FALSE.

k_random_noise

Integer. Number of standard-normal noise columns (noise1, noise2, ...) drawn once onto the super-population at construction. Default 0L (no noise columns; output identical to previous versions).

noise_seed

Integer. Seed for the population-level noise draw, used only when k_random_noise > 0. Default 20260807L, the committed population-noise seed (commit 2a4787bc).

Value

An object of class c("glm_dgm", "list") with:

df_super

Super-population data frame with potential outcome columns: p0, p1 (binary probabilities), or mu0, mu1 (conditional means for continuous / count outcomes), and flag_harm.

df_source

The observed analysis frame in observed order (every source patient exactly once), carrying the same potential-outcome columns as df_super computed by the identical prediction calls, plus flag_harm and the discretised covariates. This is the frozen panel consumed by simulate_from_glm_dgm(baseline = "fixed").

hazard_ratios

Named list with harm_subgroup, no_harm_subgroup, and overall – effect estimates on the scale determined by effect_measure. Field name retained for compatibility with get_dgm_hr() and reporting functions.

outcome_type

Character: "binary", "continuous", or "count".

effect_measure

Character: the effect measure used.

model_params

List with fitted coefficients, family, k_inter, residual SD (continuous), and offset variable name (count).

subgroup_info

List with subgroup definition, size, and proportion.

model_type

Character: "alt" or "null".

noise_names

Character vector of noise column names (character(0) when k_random_noise = 0).

noise_scheme

"population" when noise was drawn, otherwise "none".

noise_seed

The seed used for the noise draw, or NA_integer_ when none was drawn.

Details

Fits a GLM to the source data, creates a super-population with individual-level potential outcomes, and stores true subgroup effects. The returned object can be passed to simulate_from_glm_dgm for simulation studies, and is compatible with run_simulation_analysis (which dispatches on class).

Noise columns requested via k_random_noise are inert N(0,1) population attributes intended as candidate confounders; the builder never puts them in the outcome model. They are drawn once onto df_super after sampling, so simulated trials inherit them by row resampling.

See also

simulate_from_glm_dgm, calibrate_glm_interaction, generate_aft_dgm_flex

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(speff2trial)
actg <- subset(ACTG175, arms %in% c(1, 3))
actg$treat  <- 1L - as.integer(actg$arms == 1)
actg$y      <- as.integer(actg$cd420 > actg$cd40)
actg$z1     <- as.factor(ifelse(actg$age > 34, 1L, 0L))
actg$z2     <- as.factor(ifelse(actg$preanti <= 745, 1L, 0L))

dgm <- generate_glm_dgm(
  data          = actg,
  factor_vars   = c("z1", "z2"),
  outcome_var   = "y",
  treatment_var = "treat",
  outcome_type  = "binary",
  subgroup_vars = c("z1", "z2"),
  subgroup_cuts = list(z1 = 1L, z2 = 1L),
  model         = "alt",
  k_inter       = 1.0,   # additive log-odds shift for Q under treatment
  verbose       = TRUE
)
} # }
